thesis: EXEL is extended after a +40% 63-day run and trades above the mean analyst target, so consensus sees no upside while the technical reward/risk is only a modest 1.65. The last two sessions printed heavy volume (vol ratio 1.55) with the 11/10 close down from a 72.14 high, and the 11/5 reversal from 73.69 looks like supply at the 52-week high. Short interest sits just under the 15% threshold, which raises gap risk in both directions. The news feed was down, so the unexplained 10/30 gap-up and any offering, M&A or litigation risk cannot be ruled out. The regime is risk-off with QQQ below its 50- and 200-day averages, so a crowded momentum winner is vulnerable to a de-grossing move even though healthcare is currently a leading sector.
